title: What AI tools do you use?
author: olafthemanofsnow
selftext:
Hi Everyone,

I have been on my own journey developing a game with the use of AI, and it has been months in the making (but at a stage where I am really proud of what I achieved).

What i am trying to build is a catalogue of tools for each element of game design.

I have broken it down into 6 main areas:

\- Concept and pre-production 

\- Visual production (2d and 3d asset generation, animation etc)

\- tech development (level design, procedural generation, enemy AI)

\- Audio

\- Quality and Assurance

\- Publishing/growth/marketing 

I have some tools already but the idea is to create a repository that I can then share back to the community.

comments.author: Thicthor96
comments.body: Gpt, Claude, Suno (for music), sudowrite for compelling writing, runway for cutscenes/story dialogue

comments.author: StellarSoupStudio
comments.body:
Literally just Claude on the 20$ plan.

I use other regular tools as well, like Inkscape, and Reaper, and Github

I've also been having Claude make tools for me to use like a replay viewer so I can watch how players interact with my game.

replies.author: JforceG
replies.body: Thats the best way to use claude imo. Make tools to help you make the game as oppose to trying to get it to make a full game for you.

replies.author: Braunb8888
replies.body: What do those do? Inkscape and reaper?

replies.author: StellarSoupStudio
replies.body:
Inkscape is a SVG editor, it's like photoshop or gimp or illustrator, but it's focused on SVG files which are pictures made using math rather than pixels so it's really good at scaling.

Reaper is a DAW (digital audio workstation) like audacity or garage band. Its for making sound effects, music, ect.

replies.author: Braunb8888
replies.body: Ah is it like GarageBand for pc? Been dying for that. Is it free?

replies.author: StellarSoupStudio
replies.body:
Not free but there's a 60 day trial per email address and for individuals its a $60 one time payment (no subscription).

If you use it and and your game gets really big then you may have to buy the $225 commercial license which is also a one time fee.

replies.author: Moda75
replies.body: You can ise reaper for free forever

comments.author: UgglyGameStudios
comments.body:
I've been using Claude Code primarily. I had experimented with Astra when it released for a month and was impressed with that. But when it came down to it, I found that I preferred Claude. 

Recently, I've been experimenting with Tripo for 3d models for a new, more ambitious project that I am working on. But Claude was able to make low poly, ps1 era graphics pretty well. It really just takes patience to get what you want out of it.

Audio is kind of tricky in my opinion. I personally have been really unimpressed with AI generated sounds. I know a lot of people use eleven labs, but nothing felt correct to me. Instead, I went the route of using cc0 sounds that I source online. 

Publishing/growth/marketing is pretty tough for me. Cluade/GPT can give you a good gameplan, but it really does feel like a lottery a lot of the times. I use it to cut tiktoks and youtube shorts, then upload those myself.

comments.author: JforceG
comments.body:
I mostly use claude for coding. 

All the 3D modeling and stuff I do for myself. But on occassionally, I'll get claude to go into a blend file to make small edits for me.

comments.author: JBMorningstar
comments.body:
Chatgpt for reference images, research and planning
Claude for technical implementations
Meshy and tripo for modeling
Blender MCP

comments.author: SilentNinja1337
comments.body:
- Concept and pre-production
I build my first prototype in GoDot using gpt and glm.

- Visual production
My girlfriend is very good at drawing. She does the concept art, I feed it into a self hosted FLUX instance to get a image of all sides. Then into Hunyuan 3D / Tripo to get the 3D asset. For moving assets I have a rigging plugin for Blender.

- tech development 
Again glm / gpt

- audio
ElevenLabs for voice, I haven't found any good open weight alternative yet. For music I have built a tool where I can generate music by giving a theme.

- QA
Automated tests where possible. But everything is checked manually through a playtest.

comments.author: mentiondesk
comments.body: For your catalogue, diving into community discussions on Reddit, LinkedIn, or even X can reveal some hidden gem tools people are actually using. If you want to catch these conversations as they happen and spot new tools getting buzz, I’ve found ParseStream useful for surfacing those real time mentions so nothing slips through the cracks.

comments.author: getloadoutai
comments.body: Cool idea, betting the QA bucket ends up the emptiest one lol! plusfor that one the most useful thing ive seen is what stellarsoup said, having claude build you your own tools. replay viewers, debug overlays, a dumb bot that just plays your game badly for an hour.( might be worth a "build your own" column next to the actual products. are you gonna list pricing per tool too? half this stuff is $20/mo each and it stacks up fast when you're solo

comments.author: NeonCenturionSPQR
comments.body:
I use Claude code specifically, lot of quality of life features. I created a plugin specifically for Claude code to help maintain context, and create a roadmap tool, using a multi agent workflow with deterministic bookkeeping and adversarial reviewers and merge gates. 

It does moderately bloat token usage, but I've seen a huge improvement to output quality.

I've primarily tested with Godot, as Godot is most natively AI friendly with its everything is plain text methodology.

Not for everyone, still ironing out some kinks, but some may find use for it.

github.com/Palatine-Labs/coniso

replies.author: Moda75
replies.body: I have an orchestrator conversation that funnels my directives to other conversations which report back to it. My clear commands for each write a handoff note first so whenever I clear a conversation it picks right back up where it left off. The different conversations let the orchestrator know when they need to be cleared.

comments.author: Alone-Biscotti6145
comments.body:
Claude for coding, Blender and GIMP, also Codex to help with art and implementation of side features to keep things rolling quicker.

Ended up building a pretty in-depth 3D remake of COD Zombies game for browser, built with Three.js and Vite on TypeScript. Support for mobile and computer!

https://zod-combies.itch.io/zod-der-untoten

replies.author: Alone-Biscotti6145
replies.body:
For audio, I used freesounds.com (a very good site with a wide selection).

For animations and assets, I use Mixamo and Sketchfab.com.

Ai: Claude code, codex, tripo3d, Suno, elevenlab, seedance. 
Non ai (if we can Say so): unity, blender (still spend 50% of my time with it if not more), Kritika.
